item.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
item.description: Twin Travelers In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. […]

item.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
item.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyond Neptune. It may be up to 1500 km in diameter.

item.title: Rubin observatory reveals two hidden companions of the Milky Way
item.description: Preview data from the recently completed NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile point to a wave of discoveries that may complete the census of the Milky Way's neighboring galaxies—including its faintest companions.

item.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
item.description: Video: 00:03:32 BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. item.title: Exceptional tests of general relativity with GW250114
item.description: In January 2025, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration observed an exceptionally loud gravitational-wave signal: GW250114. It stands out as the clearest one observed thus far, about three times louder than the first detection in 2015.
